title: Workflows and agents: who owns the control flow

items.stem: Some systems that use a language model are called workflows and others are called agents. What decides which of the two a system is?

options.text: Whether it calls the model more than once
Whether it uses tools such as a calendar
Whether code or the model picks each next step
Whether it uses a larger, more capable model

items.stem: Design A: for every question, our code searches the manuals, passes the top three pages to the model to write an answer, then stops. Design B: the model gets search_manuals and check_calendar tools and decides what to call, how often, and when to stop. Which description is correct?

options.text: A is a workflow because code fixes the steps; B is an agent because the model picks them
A is an agent because it uses a model; B is a workflow because it uses tools
Both are agents, because in both the model writes the final answer
Both are workflows, because in both our own program runs everything

items.stem: In one short phrase: what must be true of a task's steps for a fixed workflow to be a better choice than an agent?

A fixed workflow answers each manual question with exactly 2 model calls. An agent doing the same job averages 6 model calls per question. Assume every model call costs $0.01. For 500 questions, how many more dollars does the agent cost than the workflow?
Which one of these makerspace assistant jobs is the best candidate to build as a fixed workflow rather than an agent?

options.text: Answering a vague question like "why does my print warp?"
Helping a student whose booking request clashes with others
Diagnosing a machine fault from a student's rough notes
Sending each student a reminder for today's bookings

items.stem: A teammate proposes making the whole assistant one agent "because agents are more flexible". For the steps whose order never changes, which is the strongest reply given our small model budget?

options.text: An agent can call each tool only once per request
A fixed workflow needs fewer model calls and behaves predictably
An agent cannot stop once it has started its loop
A fixed workflow can use a more capable model
